title: Nobel Laureate Michael Kremer Picked as World Bank Top Economist
summary: The World Bank Group said that Nobel laureate Michael Kremer will serve as its new chief economist starting Oct. 1, heading research for the institution, according to a statement Wednesday.

title: Stocks, Bonds Rise in Countdown to Fed Decision: Markets Wrap
summary: Stocks joined bonds higher after days of selling as oil prices fell, with traders betting the Federal Reserve will lift interest rates to fight inflation and bolster its credibility.

title: Uganda Shilling Dips to Lowest Since 2024 as FX Demand Soars
summary: Uganda’s shilling slumped to a 2-1/2 year low against the dollar, weighed down by a surge in demand for foreign-exchange in key economic sectors including energy, manufacturing and telecommunications.

title: Monaco Set to Exit Dirty-Money List Along With Bulgaria, Ivory Coast
summary: Monaco is among several nations poised to exit a global financial watchdog’s dirty money watchlist next month, marking a change in fortune for the city-state that’s home to the world’s highest concentration of millionaires and billionaires.

title: Europe Gas Fluctuates as Traders Weigh German Stockpiling Moves
summary: European natural gas fluctuated as traders weighed Germany’s next moves to boost winter stockpiles, which could determine fuel demand from the county in the coming months.

title: Zillow Loses Antitrust Battle Over Chicago Area Listings Feed
summary: Zillow Group Inc. lost its bid to force Illinois’ largest provider of real estate listings to provide access to its data about homes for sale.

title: Turkey Stocks Trigger Circuit Breaker After Fund Redemptions
summary: Turkish stocks tumbled on Wednesday and triggered a market-wide circuit breaker, as an asset manager’s failure to meet redemption requests fueled concern about broader liquidity stress in the country’s investment fund industry.

title: European Stocks Advance as Bond Yields and Oil Ease Ahead of Fed
summary: European shares snapped two days of losses as a bond selloff and oil prices eased ahead of the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision later on Wednesday.

title: Sazerac Is Said to Study Deal For German Schnapps Maker Berentzen
summary: US spirits firm Sazerac Co. is exploring a potential acquisition of German schnapps maker Berentzen-Gruppe AG, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: SEC Moves to Scrap Shareholder Proxy Proposal Rules
summary: Rules governing how shareholders in publicly-traded companies can bring corporate proposals would be scrapped under a new measure issued today by the Securities and Exchange Commission.

title: Pangestu: Indonesia May See Lower Budget Deficit in 2027
summary: Indonesian National Economic Council Vice Chair Mari Pangestu believes the country may see a lower budget deficit next year. She also expects fiscal discipline from new Finance Minister Suahasil Nazara. She speaks with Paul Allen on "Insight with Haslinda Amin." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Venezuela Plans to Ship Aluminum to US in Mercuria-Heeney Deal
summary: Venezuela is preparing to ship aluminum to the US under a deal with Mercuria Energy Group Ltd. and Heeney Capital, diversifying beyond oil in a quickening revival of commercial ties following years of economic and diplomatic isolation.

title: Unloved Consumer Names Like Walmart Face Pressure as Rate Hike Draws Near
summary: Stocks that are most closely tied to the health of the US consumer have trailed the broader market badly this year. A potential Federal Reserve interest-rate hike Wednesday may add to the segment’s stress.

title: UAE Wins Dismissal of Oil Trader’s Lawsuit Alleging Smears
summary: The United Arab Emirates won dismissal of a lawsuit by an oil trader who alleged the state directed a smear campaign that pushed his company into bankruptcy.

title: Intel-SK Hynix Potential Tie Up; JB Hunt Lower on Costs | Stock Movers
summary:
On this episode of Stock Movers:

- Intel (INTC) is the most actively traded stock in the premarket after Reuters reported that SK Hynix is in talks with the chipmaker about a deal that ​would see it manufacture memory chips in the US for the first time. SK Hynix says it’s made no decisions in response to a Reuters report that it’s in talks with Intel about a deal to make semiconductors in the US.
- JB Hunt (JBHT) shares are lower this morning after the trucking company flagged rising costs and issued a rare earnings warning at a Morgan Stanley conference. 
- Reliance Worldwide (RWC) shares are moving on news Brookfield agreed to pay $3.38 a share to buy Reliance World. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Burnham Weighs Thames Water Intervention Alongside Mayors Plan
summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is keeping radical intervention at Thames Water on the table even as he considers a separate plan to give local mayors a greater role in overseeing the troubled industry.

title: Fed Expected to Hike Rates for First Time Since 2023
summary: The Federal Reserve is expected to hike interest rates for the first time in three years on Wednesday. Investors on Tuesday saw a greater than 90% chance of a quarter-point move this week and priced in another hike by the end of the year. Michael McKee has a preview. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Retail Sales Rise 1.2% in August After Dropping in July
summary: US retail sales rose broadly in August showing that consumers are still spending despite higher gasoline prices. Twelve of 13 retail categories reported increases, boosted by back-to-school shopping. Sales were up by 1.2% beating the estimate of 0.8%. Bloomberg's Michael McKee reports from Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bond Market’s ‘Extreme’ Short Counts on Fed to Deliver Hike
summary:
Bond traders have piled into bearish positions ahead of Wednesday’s Federal Reserve meeting, betting that the Treasury selloff driving yields to their highest in almost two decades will continue. 
Steven Major, Global Macro Advisor at Tradition, discusses the case for a bond rally and falling yields. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Transforming the New York Liberty Into WNBA Champions
summary: Clara Wu Tsai sits down with David Rubenstein to discuss New York Liberty's transformation. She talks about moving the team from Westchester to the Barclays Center in Brooklyn, investing in players, facilities and management, and how it all led to winning the WNBA championship. Wu Tsai joins David Rubenstein for the premiere episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations, Season 12. This interview was recorded June 4, in Brooklyn, New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Ed Yardeni Cuts S&P 500 View to 7,900 on Downturn Risks
summary: Ed Yardeni, one of the biggest stock bulls on Wall Street, is slashing his year-end forecast for the S&P 500 Index a month after raising it, citing increasing risks of a downturn in the next three to six months.
